dedupe_keys.name: nlr sera scenario evaluation and regionalization analysis cost optimal hydrogen production delivery and refuelling infrastructure build out

description: SERA (Scenario Evaluation and Regionalization Analysis) is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) systems analysis model that designs supply chain infrastructure for hydrogen and other emerging commodities from city to national or international scale. Contents: it cost-optimises the build-out of hydrogen production, transmission, storage and distribution to meet user-defined demand, determining the number, capacity and location of production units (steam methane reforming, electrolysis, methane pyrolysis, coal or biomass gasification), estimating supply chain levelized costs and cash flows under financing and incentive schemes, and it has been applied to ammonia, sustainable aviation fuel and synthetic natural gas; earlier work covered refuelling station roll-out for fuel cell vehicles. Producer: NLR Hydrogen and Fuel Cells programme; technical reports from 2013 and 2019 describe the framework. Coverage: user-defined regions, with US and international trade analyses to 2035. Format and access: publicly available but closed source; access is by a user request and licence form and only US-based entities are granted access. Licence: closed source under an NLR licence. Caveats: not open code, and results depend on technology cost inputs. Simulation uses: siting and sizing hydrogen production, pipelines, storage and refuelling stations in energy transition scenarios. Related records: data-policy-aware-hydrogen-refuelling-reproduction and data-nlr-next-generation-hydrogen-station-composite-data-products.
